text:
## Description

Determine whether some uppercase English string of length \(N\) permits operations that turn every entry of the given binary sequence into a 1. Read the sequence from standard input and print the decision to standard output.

## Preconditions

- **PRE-1 (Unverified)** — The first input line contains an integer \(N\) with \(3 \le N \le 200000\).
- **PRE-2 (Unverified)** — The second input line contains exactly \(N\) space-separated integers, each equal to 0 or 1.

## Postconditions

- **POST-1 (Unverified)** — For a fixed candidate string, an operation is permitted at position \(i\) exactly when the three consecutive letters starting there read `ARC` or `CRA`. It sets the sequence entries at positions \(i\) and \(i+1\) to 1 and leaves all other entries and the string unchanged. Positions wrap cyclically for both the string and the sequence.
- **POST-2 (Unverified)** — The program prints `Yes` if at least one candidate string allows a finite sequence of permitted operations to leave every entry equal to 1. Zero operations are allowed, so an input consisting entirely of ones yields `Yes`. Permitted operations may be repeated or applied in any order, including when both affected entries are already 1.
- **POST-3 (Unverified)** — The program prints `No` if no candidate string can reach the all-ones state. The output consists of a single decision word, with any capitalization accepted by the judge.

## Test suggestions

- Check that `0 0 0` yields `No` and `0 1 0` yields `Yes` at \(N=3\). For the second case, `RCA` permits an operation starting at position 3 that covers both zeros. (PRE-1, PRE-2, POST-1, POST-2, POST-3)
- Check that an all-ones sequence at \(N=200000\) yields `Yes`. (PRE-1, PRE-2, POST-2)
- Check that the first sample yields `Yes`. Its supplied witness uses both permitted letter patterns. (POST-1, POST-2)

## Unspecified behavior

Handling malformed input or values outside the stated constraints is unspecified. The task prescribes no choice of witness string or operation sequence when several exist.
